headline: Inferring tumor clonal structure and selection from single-cell RNA-seq readouts
label: Single Cell Clonal Evolution Inference
summary: scRNA-seq readouts now identify tumor cell populations and oncogene-carrying ecDNA, extending clonal inference to extrachromosomal DNA.
synthesis: The common thread across these items is inferring tumor clonal structure and selection from single-cell RNA-seq readouts. SCANBIT pools transcriptionally similar scRNA-seq clusters to call SNVs and uses bootstrapped hierarchical clustering to identify tumor cell populations. ecSingle applies related logic to extrachromosomal DNA, inferring oncogene-carrying ecDNA from allelic imbalance and outlier expression to resolve ecDNA clonal evolution and selection at single-cell resolution. The distinct contribution of ecSingle is recovering oncogene-carrying ecDNA from scRNA-seq allelic imbalance and expression outliers, placing extrachromosomal elements within the same single-cell framework. PanCNV-Explorer is orthogonal in scope: it provides a unified database of harmonized copy number variation data across 33 cancer types, cell lines, and healthy cohorts, accessible through a web browser. Together, the items pair single-cell variant and ecDNA inference with a harmonized copy number resource.
